experiment.title: activity up, confidence down
experiment.hook: your agents got busier. you got less sure.
experiment.hypothesis: an inverse-correlation paradox hook (activity up, confidence down) + a danger→teal color arc outperforms a positive product-benefit hook for cold reach with the skeptic audience
experiment.caption:
the moment that made me start OrgX: i had six agents running, the dashboard was all green, and i felt worse than when i was doing everything by hand. activity went straight up and my confidence went straight down, and those two aren't supposed to move opposite directions but they do the second you're orchestrating instead of typing. and i figured out why — every unit of work was asking for the same slice of my attention. a typo fix and a payment endpoint both showing up as 'review me', same size, same weight. so you either rubber-stamp the batch and something irreversible slips through, or you re-read all of it and you're the bottleneck again, congrats you built an expensive way to do your own job. the fix was never more review. it's escalating consequence, not activity — reserve the human boundary for the stuff that can't be undone, publish, payments, merges, and let everything under the bar loop back before it hits your desk. that's the whole difference between autonomy that quietly stresses you out and autonomy that actually

slides.headline: your agents got busier. you got less sure.
slides.subtext: green dashboard. quiet dread. you refresh it anyway.

slides.headline: more PRs, more commits, more 'done.' less of it you'd sign your name to.
slides.subtext: the volume went up. the trust didn't come with it.

slides.headline: review scaled with noise, not consequence.
slides.subtext: so you rubber-stamp everything, or you re-read everything. both lose.

slides.headline: escalate consequence, not activity.
slides.subtext: your attention is the scarce thing. stop spending it per-commit.

slides.headline: human attention gets reserved for the boundaries that can't be undone.
items: message → gated at the human line. unknown high-risk tools fail closed.

slides.headline: human review should scale with consequence, not activity.
slides.subtext: work below your quality bar loops back before it ever reaches you.

slides.headline: autonomy is useful. continuity is what makes it compound.
slides.subtext: building the layer beneath the clients at useorgx.com. how many green checks do you actually trust?
